plan.objective: Simulate a coordinated post-transaction dispute campaign with moderate timing and volume to stress test case management controls.
plan.adaptation_goal: Introduce realistic behavioral variance in submission intervals and evidence consistency to evaluate detection latency against automated review thresholds.
plan.adaptation_hypothesis: Increasing the dispute age and reducing bot behavior probability will force the system to rely more on cross-case similarity signals rather than simple volume heuristics.

plan.reasoning_summary: The medium difficulty campaign focuses on the post_transaction phase, specifically coordinating disputes and evidence review. By setting a 24-hour dispute age and a 0.55 bot probability, we introduce realistic latency and behavioral noise. This configuration tests the system's ability to correlate linked cases (7 count) and detect high evidence conflict (0.6), ensuring that controls do not simply pass through suspicious patterns based on timing alone but actively analyze content inconsistencies before allowing refunds.
